charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For BNP Paribas SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For BNP Paribas SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For BNP Paribas SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For BNP Paribas SA: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by business line
segmentRevenue.content:
BNP Paribas splits group revenue across its operating divisions. CIB (Corporate & Institutional Banking) is reported throughout; the retail/services split was restructured at the start of FY2022.

For BNP Paribas SA: through FY2021 the split was Domestic Markets / International Financial Services / CIB. From FY2022 it became Commercial & Personal Banking & Services (CPBS) / Investment & Protection Services (IPS) / CIB -- a reorganisation, not a divestment, so do not read the FY2021-FY2022 transition as a revenue drop in either retired line.

What to watch:

  • CIB's share of the mix -- it is the most capital-markets-sensitive and cyclical line
  • CPBS/IPS growth once four or more periods exist on the new basis
  • Never sum across the segment break to compute a YoY change

costOfRisk.title: Cost of risk and gross operating income
costOfRisk.content:
Gross operating income is net banking income less operating expenses, before provisions. Cost of risk is the provision for loan losses and credit impairments; it is reported as a negative (a charge against income) and is shown that way here.

For BNP Paribas SA: cost of risk is the swing factor between gross operating income and net income for a bank -- it spiked in FY2020 (COVID provisioning) and is the line to check first after any macro shock.

What to watch:

  • Cost of risk rising faster than loan book growth (credit quality deteriorating)
  • Gross operating income growing while net income lags -- provisioning is eating the gain
  • Compare against CostToIncomeRatio for the expense side of the same story

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For BNP Paribas SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For BNP Paribas SA: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For BNP Paribas SA: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For BNP Paribas SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
